title: Brian Schottenheimer: “We’re in Win-Now Mode”
headline: Cowboys traded for CB Joey Porter Jr., who moved well in his first practice and could play this week vs. Houston in a limited, specially designed package.
summary: Schottenheimer framed the Joey Porter Jr. trade as proof of Dallas's win-now approach, crediting Jerry Jones, Stephen Jones and Will McClay for being aggressive. He praised Porter's length, size, physicality and elite cover skills, plus his ability to fill against the run and tackle. Porter had back issues in Pittsburgh, but the coach said he moved well in his first practice. Schottenheimer wouldn't commit to Porter playing this week, saying the team would like him to and will see how the week goes. Defensive coordinator Christian Parker has a specific plan for Porter, which Schottenheimer wouldn't reveal because the Texans will be watching. He said Porter probably won't play every snap, but if he plays there will be a good package for him, and the team doesn't yet know where he'll line up. He said the addition helps a secondary depleted by injuries and also helps the pass rush by tightening coverage and disrupting timing. He also said Dak Prescott is still playing at an elite level and the offense has elite weapons.

injuries.detail: Had back issues in Pittsburgh. Moved around well in his first Dallas practice, and the team would like him to play this week but is waiting to see how the week goes.

signals.claim: Will have a specific defensive package if he plays this week against Houston, though probably not every snap.
signals.note: For IDP and DST managers, an elite corner added to a depleted secondary could improve Dallas's coverage and pass-rush outlook.
signals.quote: if he plays, we'll certainly have a good package for him.

signals.claim: Porter's availability for the game this week will be decided as the week goes on.
signals.note: His back history and the coach's refusal to commit make his Week status uncertain, so check later practice reports.
signals.quote: We'd like him to play, but we'll see how the week goes.

signals.note: The coach cited Prescott's elite level of play as a reason for the win-now stance, which supports confidence in the offense.
signals.quote: Dak Prescott still playing at elite level.

topics.detail: Schottenheimer said he and Jerry Jones have been aligned on a win-now approach from the start. He cited Jones's age, Dak Prescott's play, elite offensive weapons and an improving defense.
Dallas's defensive backs group is depleted by injuries, and Porter adds an elite-coverage young corner. The team communicated with players in the DB room about the trade before it was finalized.
Tight coverage disrupts timing and helps the rush get home. Disguised coverages and fewer open receivers should help, though the team still has to finish sacks by wrapping up and tackling.

Schottenheimer said the trade had little to do with the loss in Brazil and was more about adding a young elite corner. He said Porter arrived early in the day, passed his physical and practiced the same day.

title: Matt LaFleur on the new offensive linemen: 'It's exciting to get them out there'
headline: Packers LaFleur wants to lean on the run vs. Tampa's stingy front, is noncommittal on committee vs. lead back, and is ramping up newly added veteran offensive linemen.
summary: LaFleur said the newly added offensive linemen did well in their first day and are veterans who have played a lot of football at a high level. Their physical readiness is a question, so the team has an individualized ramp-up plan for each one, which he refused to share for competitive reasons. He stressed the need to get the run game going because it opens up the whole offense and keeps defenses from keying on one dimension, while acknowledging Tampa Bay has one of the stingiest run defenses, led by Vita Vea. He said the short, quick passing game can supplement the run by any means necessary, but man-heavy 'matchy' coverages make it harder. Asked about the backfield, he said there are benefits to both a three-man committee with defined roles and a lead dog, and he did not commit to a change. He expects the defense to respond positively after last week and called Tampa's offensive line one of the league's better ones. He also praised Bucky Irving as a top-tier tailback and noted the Bucs have a rookie quarterback the Packers know little about.

signals.note: LaFleur would not commit to moving away from the backfield committee, so Jacobs' workload is unsettled, though a lead-back approach was acknowledged as having benefits.

signals.claim: The offense wants to lean more on the run game and short, quick passing to supplement it.
signals.note: A run-leaning plan against a tough front and quick-game usage could cap Love's downfield volume this week.

topics.detail: The new veteran linemen had a good first day. The team has individualized ramp-up plans, and the coaches teach them from the weekly game plan rather than the full playbook. Protection calls and code words are the main learning curve.

LaFleur wants to get the run game going to keep the defense from keying on the pass, though Tampa's run defense is among the league's stingiest. Short, quick passing can supplement it, but man-heavy coverages make that harder.
He sees pluses and minuses in both a three-man committee with defined roles and a single lead back, and did not announce any change.

He praised Vita Vea and the Bucs' edge setters, physical linebackers and secondary. He called their offensive line one of the league's better units and Bucky Irving a top-tier tailback. They have a rookie quarterback the Packers don't know much about.
He expects the defense to respond positively after last week and said Wednesday's practice was great.
He would not want replay review of pass interference to return, preferring consistent officiating.
